_comment: Line library for the J-54 host (v2 table, docs/design/J54_V2_SPEC.md). Each event holds alternative scripts; one is picked at random. A script is a list of [expression, text] beats; expressions are J-54's portraits (resting_mania, grand_welcome, card_reveal, secretive_trick, obsessive_lecture, paranoid_analysis, guarded, irritated, glitching_frenzy). victory.capture replaces victory when the run is won by capturing the Joker. summary_mood is used for the protocol lines the table generates. In-round lines (a condition begins, the Joker is released) are the persona's table_condition / table_release lines in ai/personas/j54.json. onboarding holds the first-visit explanations, one script per milestone (docs/design/TUTORIAL.md section 8, chaos_blackjack/j54/onboarding.py); {braced} names are the profile's numbers, filled in at the table.
profile: J-54 is a calculating machine built as a circus clown. It performs every gesture as if for a full tent, then reports the result in the voice of a compiler.

It never touches your cards. It changes what its own cards are worth, one condition at a time, and leaves you a little compute to rebuild the deck it deals from. Somewhere in that deck, sealed, is the sample it wants back.
signature: Fifty-four cards. Infinite configurations. One correct one.
intro: Welcome, welcome! Step into the ring. Experiment J-54 initialised.
One deck for the whole run. I set the conditions. You spend the compute. We will see which of us reads the cards better.
Ladies, gentlemen, test subjects. J-54, at your service.
My conditions touch only my cards. Yours you may rearrange. Within budget.
New operator detected. Loading fifty-two cards. One Joker: sealed.
Sealed. For now. Ha. Ha. Ha.
Protocol: sixteen rounds, one condition at a time, compute credited every round.
The meter shows which way the deck leans. It does not tell you what to do. Neither will I.

j54_intro_table: Orientation protocol. One deck lasts the whole run. Every round I shuffle all of it, and only the two of us change what is in it.
The strip on the right is that deck, rank by rank, coloured by heat. Green: removing those cards helps you. Red: keep them. The colours follow my conditions.

Compute: +{compute_income} every round, {compute_cap} at most. Cut takes {cut_size} cards of the rank and colour you name: precise. Hot Purge takes {hot_purge_size} of one of the hottest ranks, drawn at random: cheap and coarse.
Your chips count toward the goal from round {target_from_round}. The other exit is my sealed Joker. Remember it. I will.
j54_intro_firmware: Before round one: firmware. One rule on your cards, never mine, for the whole run.
It is paid from your starting chips, now; the price is on each option. The meter and the heat strip count it from the first hand.
No firmware is a fair pick. You keep every chip and your cards count as printed.
j54_intro_condition: Announcement detected. My condition in force is in the rules panel. It changes what my cards are worth, or when I stand. Never yours.
Every condition has a camp. Classic leans the way plain blackjack does, anti the other way, and the loner goes its own way.
When the camp switches, the heat strip turns around: green may go red. That is why I name the next camp one round ahead.
Compute held now can be spent on the new map instead of the old one. Your call. I log both.
j54_intro_release: Compute at {release_cost}. Release is within budget.

Release puts my sealed Joker into the deck for the rest of the run. For you it is a soft ace. Hold it when a hand you do not lose settles, from round {capture_from_round}, and the experiment ends in your favour.
A thin deck makes the draw likelier. If I draw it myself, I shuffle it back and add a low card to the deck. Ha. Ha.

victory: Capital threshold reached. That was not the projected outcome.
You read my conditions and cut accordingly.
Logging this as an anomaly. Return so I can correct it.
Result recorded: the subject outperformed the program.
victory.capture: The sample is in your hand. Capture confirmed.
I sealed it for a reason. Logging the reason as insufficient.
Experiment complete. The sample belongs to the subject. This is noted.
Fifty-three cards, one of them mine, and you held it.
Bravo! The ring applauds. I compute.
defeat: Funds exhausted. The experiment ends here.
For your next run: compute held is compute wasted.
Round sixteen settled. No capital. No capture.
The Joker was in the deck. Statistically, it was almost yours.
Resetting the deck to fifty-two. Same time again?
The meter pointed one way. You bet the other.
